summary:
Backend Tutorials feature is in place and the full suite passes (104 tests).

**What I added**, following the existing Reminders vertical-slice structure:

- `src/CleanArchitecture.Domain/Tutorials/Tutorial.cs` — entity with `Id`, `Title`, `Description`, `Published`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt` and an `Update(...)` method that bumps `UpdatedAt`.
- `src/CleanArchitecture.Contracts/Tutorials/` — `CreateTutorialRequest`, `UpdateTutorialRequest`, `TutorialResponse`, `MessageResponse` (field names match the contract exactly; default camelCase serialization yields `id/title/description/published/createdAt/updatedAt` and `message`).
- `src/CleanArchitecture.Application/Tutorials/` — MediatR commands/handlers (Create, Update, Delete, DeleteAll) with FluentValidation validators, and queries (GetTutorial, ListTutorials with optional `Title` filter). These are plain `IRequest<ErrorOr<T>>` so the authorization pipeline behavior doesn't apply — tutorials are unauthenticated, matching the frontend service which sends no token.
- `src/CleanArchitecture.Application/Common/Interfaces/ITutorialsRepository.cs` + `src/CleanArchitecture.Infrastructure/Tutorials/Persistence/` — repository and EF configuration; `DbSet<Tutorial>` on `AppDbContext`, registered in `AddPersistence`.
- `src/CleanArchitecture.Api/Controllers/TutorialsController.cs` — `[AllowAnonymous]`, route `api/tutorials`: `GET` (with `?title=`), `GET /{id}`, `POST`, `PUT /{id}` (returns `{ message }`), `DELETE /{id}`, `DELETE`. Missing ids return 404 via the existing `ApiController.Problem` mapping of `ErrorType.NotFound`.
- CORS policy for `http://localhost:4200` in `AddPresentation` + `app.UseCors(...)` in `Program.cs`. The API already listens on `http://localhost:5001`.
- `Migrations/20261027000000_AddTutorials.cs` + Designer, and the updated `AppDbContextModelSnapshot` — hand-authored because `dotnet ef migrations add` was not permitted to run in this sandbox; the SQL shape matches what the configuration produces (verified indirectly by the integration tests, which build the schema from the same model).
- Tests: `TestCommon` factories/constants for tutorials, domain unit tests, subcutaneous tests for every command/query, and `TutorialsControllerTests` covering the full HTTP surface including the 404 and the `?title=` filter. No hard-coded calendar dates — all dates derive from `DateTime.UtcNow` or the injected `IDateTimeProvider`.

Interpretation I took: feature 1 (Tutorials API) is backend work and I implemented it fully; feature 2 (the Tutorial Details Drawer) and pointing `tutorial.service.ts` at `http://localhost:5001/api` via an environment file and `api.interceptor.ts` are frontend work and were left for the counterpart repository.
blockers: Not applied -- Tutorial Details Drawer (side drawer with Publish/Unpublish, Delete, edit link, 'Not found' on 404): Frontend work - belongs to the counterpart Angular repository, which is not checked out here

Not applied -- Point tutorial.service.ts at http://localhost:5001/api using an environment file and api.interceptor.ts: Frontend work - belongs to the counterpart Angular repository; the backend already listens on http://localhost:5001 and serves the routes under /api

Not applied -- Run `dotnet ef migrations add` to generate the migration: The command required interactive approval in this sandbox; the migration, Designer and model snapshot were hand-authored to match the EF model instead

endpoints.purpose: List tutorials filtered by title query string
Fetch one tutorial; 404 ProblemDetails when not found
Create a tutorial; 201 Created with Location header
Update a tutorial / toggle published; 200 with message
Delete one tutorial; 204 No Content with empty body
Delete all tutorials; 200 with count message

context_sharing.notes: All seven endpoints the frontend asked for are implemented. Routes live under 'api/tutorials' (controller [Route("api/tutorials")]), so with the interceptor base of http://localhost:5001/api the relative path '/tutorials' is correct. id is a GUID serialized as a string, not a number; createdAt/updatedAt are ISO-8601 UTC datetime strings. The {tutorialId} route segment is constrained to :guid, so a non-GUID id yields 404 route-miss rather than a ProblemDetails. POST returns the full created tutorial (201) rather than an empty body, and DELETE /tutorials (all) returns {message} while DELETE /tutorials/{id} returns 204 with no body. Errors are RFC7807 ProblemDetails; validation failures on POST/PUT return 400 (title required, max 200 chars; description non-null, max 10000). CORS only allows origin http://localhost:4200.
